newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: Czech real May ind output -3.3 pct yr/yr (+8.2 pct).
newsitem.headline: Czech real May ind output -3.3 pct yr/yr (+8.2 pct).

text.p: Czech real industrial output in May fell 3.3 percent, year-on-year, putting real output for the first five months of the year down 2.5 percent year-on-year, the statistical bureau (CSU) said on Thursday.
It added that average industrial monthly wages grew, in nominal terms, 11.9 percent, year-on-year, in May after 14.7 percent growth in April.
The CSU also said that real construction output for May grew by 2.0 percent, year-on-year, after 5.9 percent year-on-year growth in April.
The CSU said industrial sales for May, in real terms, fell by 0.7 percent, year-on-year.
NOTE. The average nominal industrial wage in May was 11,153 crowns compared with 10,357 in April.

In January, the CSU changed its methodology for calculating industrial production. The new methodology excludes multiple calculation of semi-finished products, resources, and other materials and commodities, which were included in output data at every stage under the old method measuring the gross value of all goods produced.
The new index measures output changes by units, weight or other measurements, of the total of 1,304 products out of 879 product groups consisting of one or more similar products.

The product groups's output indices are placed in sectors, using weighting equal to their weight in the respective sector. The overall index is calculated from weighted changes in the sectoral indices.
